newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end sharply up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end sharply up in thin trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock futures ended on Monday at their highest level this year, aided by a recovery in Tokyo blue chips, but activity was subdued ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting, dealers said.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract added 160 points to end at 20,535 on low volume of 11,287 lots.
"Technically, the Nikkei looks good. But the worry is that if the Fed tightens rates, it may give the Bank of Japan more room to manoeuvre," a trader with a local futures house said.
The Fed's policy-making arm was due to meet on Tuesday and sentiment is divided over whether the U.S. central bank would raise rates for the second time this year.
The trader said the June Nikkei looked well supported around 20,250-20,300 and could test that region again before heading higher, towards a target of 20,750.
He said activity had been dominated by intra-day traders as the larger institutional players bided their time and awaited the outcome of the Fed meeting.
The May MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 348.8 against its opening 348.4 on volume of 482 lots.
